# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Remove the old vocabularies `packs/claudinite-tasks` still decodes:

- `task-contract.mjs` — `LEGACY_FIELDS` (`agent_preprocessing*`, `prework*`, `after`),
  `LEGACY_OUTCOMES`, and `SESSION_SCOPES` (the retired `self`/`fleet` field, kept only so a
  declaration still carrying it validates).
- `run-record.mjs` — `LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES`.
- `queue/work-item.mjs` — the `task:*` label constants, `LEGACY_STATUS`, `LEGACY_PARK_RE`,

- `calendar.mjs` — `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES`, already an empty frozen object.
- `tasks/usage-fold/usage-format.mjs` — `renameLegacyCounters`.

**Two different gates, and they clear at different times.** The contract fields and
`SESSION_SCOPES` are held by a member's own local-pack task declarations — the Shepherd row.
The label vocabulary and the delivered-PR headings are held by *open work items* in every
member's issue tracker, which drain on their own as items close; the counter rename is held by
folded rows inside the retention window, so it clears when the oldest row in the window
postdates the rename.

Removing a decoder before its rows drain does not error — it silently writes `null` where the old
rows counted, and only for the old rows.

**Before touching anything**: `git clone --depth 1` missingbulb/Shepherd, read
`fleet-legacy-tolerances.GENERATED.md`, and for the label half confirm no member has an open work
item wearing a `task:` label. If a gate is not clear, comment what you read, rewrite `Not-before:`
to 14 days out, and leave this open.

**The policy is the prediction**: this stays inside `packs/claudinite-tasks`. If the diff reaches
`engine/` or another pack, the PR parks — that is the signal that the vocabulary was not as
contained as this brief assumed, not something to route around by widening the policy.

**Done looks like**: no `LEGACY_` binding remains in the pack, the pack's version is bumped with
its `VERSIONS.md` row, and the suite is green. Comment the evidence on #1638, then close as
completed.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

repos that use it — which are active, which are inert, which stopped converging months ago — and
building a census so a removal could wait on it makes the canon depend on exactly the thing it
cannot see. A gate phrased as "no member still carries the shape" is one that can never read
true, so the tolerance it guards stands forever.

behaving correctly picks the advisory up and cleans up after itself within a week, and a repo
that has not converged in a week is not being served by this canon whatever a census would have
said about it. Later this may ride major version releases instead.

<!-- link of #1638 -->

Remove the tolerances that let a member's declaration or stamp be read in its pre-rename shape:

- `engine/settings-file-names.mjs` — `LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE` (`.claudinite-checks.json`) and its
  presence in `SETTINGS_FILES`, plus every reader that iterates the pair.
- `engine/installed-versions.mjs` — `LEGACY_STAMP_KEY` (the `claudinite` stamp block).
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs` — `LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS` (`claudinite`, `maintenance`,
  including the `maintenance.delivery` → `requirePrReview` fold), `LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY`
  (`taskScheduler.endpoints`), and the top-level `packConfig` overlay.
- `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs` — `LEGACY_LOCAL_DECL_PREFIX` (`local_packs/`) and the
  `@deprecated` `LEGACY_LOCAL_PACKS_SUBDIR` export.
- `engine/version.mjs` — the integer-version branch of `parseVersion` and `isLegacyVersion`.
- `engine/migrations/registry.mjs` — the alias plumbing that exists only for the above.

**The gate is the window, and it has already passed when you pick this up.** The advisory
(`legacy-shape-in-use`) shipped when #1637 closed; this issue releases a week later, which is
the time a correctly-behaving repo needs to converge, read its own finding and clean up after
itself. Do not go looking for a census of who still holds the shape — the canon cannot see which
repos are active, inert or long-abandoned, and a removal that waits on that answer waits forever.
A repo that has not converged in a week is not being served by this canon.

**Why `Automerge: nothing` and why it must not be widened.** A repo that missed the window does
not get a degraded mount — it gets an unreadable one, and the `update` task that would deliver
its own repair is exactly what it loses. That is past what a later PR undoes, so this diff is
read by a person however small it turns out to be.

**Done looks like**: no `LEGACY_` export above survives, `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`
is green, and the migration records that documented these renames are dropped or reduced to the
write-side rewrite alone. Comment the evidence on #1638, then close as completed.

input.body:
Tracker for removing every legacy tolerance the engine and packs still carry. The mechanism that
makes each one visible and annotated is #1637; this is the removal half.

## What is still tolerated

| Family | Sites | What holds the old shape |
|---|---|---|
| Member declaration & stamp | `engine/settings-file-names.mjs`, `engine/installed-versions.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`, `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs`, `engine/version.mjs` | a repo's `.claudinite-checks.json` name, `claudinite`/`maintenance` blocks, top-level `packConfig`, `taskScheduler.endpoints`, `local_packs/` declaration prefix, integer versions in a stamp |
| Renamed / absorbed pack ids | `engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs` | a repo declaring `core`, `grow_with_claudinite`, `sheepdog`, `canary-probe`, `chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions`, `firebase-release` |
| Task contract & queue vocabulary | `packs/claudinite-tasks/task-contract.mjs`, `run-record.mjs`, `queue/work-item.mjs`, `queue/secrets-bag.mjs`, `tasks/usage-fold/` | a repo's local-pack task declaring `agent_preprocessing`/`prework`/`after`/`self`; open work items wearing `task:*` labels; folded counters under old keys |
| Assorted residues | `packs/chrome-extension/worldRules/release-workflows.mjs`, `engine/served-by.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/engine-update.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-tasks/calendar.mjs`, `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` | a repo's release workflow, `servedBy: updates`, a stale vendored worker, a repo's `declared-checks.json` spellings |

## The gate is a window, not a census

*(Owner decision, 2026-09-03 — this replaces the plan's original first link, #1639, which is
closed.)*

Every one of these was originally gated on "no member still carries the shape", and the canon
cannot answer that: it does not know which repos that use it are active, which are inert, and
which stopped converging months ago. A gate phrased that way can never read true, which is how a
tolerance becomes permanent while looking scheduled.

So each removal is gated on a **convergence window** instead. The advisory ships with #1637; a
repo behaving correctly converges, sees its own finding and cleans up after itself within a week;
a week later the link releases and the tolerance comes out. A repo that has not converged in a
week is not being served by this canon whatever a census would have said. Later this may ride
major version releases instead.

Two decoders are the exception, and only because their gate is readable *here*: the `task:*`
labels drain as open work items close, and the folded counters drain with the retention window.
#1642 reads those two locally.

Getting a window wrong is not symmetric. For the first two families a repo that missed it gets
**no pack** rather than a degraded one, loses the `update` task that would have delivered its own
repair, and the only route back is a hand-run against that repo (`renamed-packs.mjs` states this).
Those two are `Automerge: nothing` whatever their diff looks like. #1642 carries a narrow
predicted-folder policy; #1643 stays `nothing` because it spans four packs by construction.

## The chain

- [ ] #1637 — the guideline, the site annotation and the advisories that tell a holder to move
- [x] ~~#1639 — fleet clearance report~~ — closed, not planned: see above
- [ ] #1640 — member declaration & stamp shapes
- [ ] #1641 — renamed / absorbed pack ids
- [ ] #1642 — task contract & queue vocabulary
- [ ] #1643 — assorted residues

Each removal is an ad-hoc queue item behind #1637 with `Not-before: 2026-09-10`. Nothing here is
on anyone's memory, and nothing waits on an answer the canon cannot get.

Append-only below this line while the chain runs.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.

  use, and with its removal already a link in the migration's chain, gated on a condition that
  reads back true rather than on a date. (2)""",
  """- **Adding a legacy tolerance** (a dual read, an accepted old spelling, a shim) — it is

  window after that advisory reaches the holders. (2)""")

# ------------------------------------------------- basics: the skill's third bullet
E('packs/basics/skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md',
  """- **The gate that releases it** — a condition that *reads back true*: "no member's declaration or
  stamp still carries the spelling", "the oldest row in the retention window postdates the
  rename". Never a date. A date is a guess about other people's convergence, and the two ways it
  is wrong are a tolerance retired while somebody still needed it, and a date that quietly passes
  with the code still there. Where the gate is genuinely unreadable from the repo that must act on
  it, making it readable is the chain's *first* link — not a caveat in the removal's brief.""",
  """- **The window that releases it** — how long a correctly-behaving holder needs to pick the
  advisory up and act on it, written as the date the removal link waits on. The tempting
  alternative is a census — "when no holder still carries the old shape" — and it is usually
  unanswerable: a project cannot see which of the things consuming it are live, which are
  dormant and which stopped updating months ago, so the removal waits on an answer that never
  arrives and the tolerance becomes permanent while looking scheduled. Read a count only where
  you own both sides of it and it really does come back ("the oldest row in the retention window
  postdates the rename"). Everywhere else, pick the window, say in the link what it assumes, and
  let a holder that ignored the advisory for that long take the break.""")

# --------------------------------------------- basics: the phase exit-condition example
E('packs/basics/skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md',
  """- **Each phase names its exit condition**, observable and stated as a thing that reads back true —
  not "cutover done" but "every member's stamp shows the new ref".""",
  """- **Each phase names its exit condition**, observable and stated as a thing that reads back true
  from where the phase runs — not "cutover done" but "the new field is in the rendered output on

  """- **(RULES-2)** An audit of this repo's own tree (#1637) found ~28 legacy declaration sites across

  feature. Reaffirm while tolerances can be added without a removal link; retire if a mechanism
  makes the omission impossible.""",
  """- **(RULES-2)** An audit of this repo's own tree (#1637) found ~28 legacy declaration sites across

}
row_re = re.compile(r'^\| (\d+\.\d+) \| ([\d-]+) \| (.*) \|$')
for pack, marks in mine.items():
    v=f'packs/{pack}/VERSIONS.md'
    lines=open(v).read().split('\n')
    idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if any(m in l for m in marks)]
    assert len(idx)==len(marks), (pack, idx)
    others=[row_re.match(l).group(1) for i,l in enumerate(lines) if row_re.match(l) and i not in idx]
    key=lambda s:tuple(int(x) for x in s.split('.'))
    top=max(others, key=key)
    day, seq = top.split('.')
    rows=[lines[i] for i in idx]                       # oldest-last order preserved
    for off, i in enumerate(reversed(idx)):            # renumber bottom-up
        newv=f'{day}.{int(seq)+off+1}'
        lines[i]=row_re.sub(lambda m: f'| {newv} | {m.group(2)} | {m.group(3)} |', lines[i])
    # move my rows to the top of the table, newest first
    mineRows=[lines[i] for i in idx]
    for i in sorted(idx, reverse=True): del lines[i]
    hdr=next(i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('|---'))
    lines[hdr+1:hdr+1]=list(reversed(sorted(mineRows, key=lambda l: key(row_re.match(l).group(1)))))
    open(v,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
    newest=row_re.match(mineRows[0]).group(1) if len(mineRows)==1 else max((row_re.match(r).group(1) for r in mineRows), key=key)
    m=f'packs/{pack}/pack.mjs'; s=open(m).read()
    s=re.sub(r"version: '\d+\.\d+',", f"version: '{newest}',", s, count=1)

input.body:
A legacy tolerance was the one thing this corpus could add with no removal written and nothing
telling its holders to move. The audit found ~28 declaration sites across `engine/` and `packs/`;
none warned anybody, and `engine/version.mjs` carried a stated end date that had passed six days
earlier with nothing arranged to notice.

Make legacy behave like deprecated:

- **Guideline (portable, `packs/basics`)** — a legacy tolerance ships as scaffolding: with its
  removal already written into the migration's chain, with a stated retirement window, and with
  an advisory that reaches whoever still holds the old shape.
- **Annotation + check (this repo's local pack)** — every legacy tolerance declaration carries
  `@legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule|none> retire:#<issue>` on the line above it, so a tolerance
  cannot exist without a scheduled removal, and `grep` is its registry.
- **Advisories** — coded advisory rules that fire in a member's own repo when its declaration,
  stamp, or task declarations still carry a legacy shape, naming the migration in the fix.

The retirement of the tolerances themselves is #1638.

**Follow-up:** the gate wording landed here as "a condition that reads back true, never a date",
and the owner reversed that the same day — the canon will never know the state of the repos that
use it, so removals ride a convergence window instead. That correction is its own change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

{"number":1645,"title":"Legacy behaves like deprecated: the guideline, the annotation, and the advisories","body":"Closes #1637

A legacy tolerance was the one thing this corpus could add with no removal written and nothing
telling its holders to move. The audit found ~28 declaration sites across `engine/` and `packs/`;
none warned anybody, and `engine/version.mjs` carried a stated end date that had passed six days
earlier with nothing arranged to notice.

## The guideline (`packs/basics`, portable)

`RULES.md` gains one rule — a tolerance is scaffolding: it ships with an advisory firing where the
old shape is still in use, and with its removal already a link in the migration's chain, gated on a
condition that reads back true rather than on a date. The *Planning a migration* bullet names that
removal among the code written before approval, and `writing-migration-plans` gains the section
behind it: the three things that ship with a tolerance, why a date gate fails in both directions,
making an unreadable gate the chain's **first link** rather than a caveat in the removal's brief,
and the asymmetry that decides between a narrow policy and `nothing`.

## The advisories — the half that reaches the holders

| Rule | Reads | Reports |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy-shape-in-use` (lifecycle) | the repo's own declaration and stamp | retired file name, `claudinite`/`maintenance` blocks, top-level `packConfig`, `taskScheduler.endpoints`, the `local_packs/` prefix, a renamed pack id, an integer version, the `updates` alias |
| `legacy-task-fields` (tasks) | `tasks//task.mjs` **source** | `agent_preprocessing*`, `prework*`, `after`, and the one-word outcome ceilings |
| `legacy-check-spellings` (growth) | `declared-checks.json` | the pre-merge `eachValueInParsedArray` spelling |
| `cer/release-workflows` (chrome-extension) | the orchestrator | its tolerated `@main` shape, which used to return silently |

All advisory, permanently: the old shape works, so none of these may stop a member's build. Each
names the edit that moves the repo forward. The task rule reads *source* because the contract's
door renames the fields away before anything downstream can see them — which is exactly what made
that tolerance invisible. Engine constants are namespace-imported and `typeof`-guarded: the two
lanes converge on separate cycles, so a pack sits beside an engine that predates a symbol, and
there the advisory simply drops rather than faulting the pack.

## The annotation — the half that schedules the removal

Every legacy declaration now carries `// @legacy-tolerance advisory: retire:#`
directly above it, so `grep -rn '@legacy-tolerance' engine packs` **is** the register.
`legacy-tolerance-scheduled` (local pack, blocking after its grace) holds both halves: a tolerance
with nothing above it, and an annotation the register cannot parse. It anchors at column 0, which
is what tells a tolerance point from a `const legacy =` inside a function, and its test runs it
against the real tree rather than only a fixture.

`advisory:none` claims no member file can hold the old shape; the local pack's rule obliges the
retire issue to say what does read the holder instead.

## The removals

#1638 tracks them as four links, each an ad-hoc queue item behind #1639 (the one human step: the
fleet clearance report has to exist in Shepherd before anything here can read a gate) with a
`Not-before:` giving the fleet a month of converges. #1640 and #1641 are `Automerge: nothing` —
a member holding a retired spelling gets *no* pack, loses the `update` task that would deliver its
repair, and the only way back is a hand-run against that repo. #1642 carries a narrow
predicted-folder policy; #1643 stays `nothing` because it spans four packs by construction.

`engine/version.mjs`' tolerance is re-gated here on the fleet's own state rather than the date it
missed.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3127 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world` 0 blocking,
`ci-work-scope` clean. Each new check was seen failing before it was believed: the annotation check
against a stripped annotation in `settings-file-names.mjs`, and `legacy-shape-in-use`'s test with
two of its branches disabled (3 of 11 tests failed).
